summary: Even the jokey "prometheus through the eyes of the american laborer" read points to what works: mythic madness, disgusting texture, and two performances going so hard the whole island feels cursed by ego.
good_pick_if: you want something intense, weird, and aggressively atmospheric
maybe_skip_if: you want clarity, normal behavior, or emotional ease

summary: The best description is that you do not notice "the darkness into which you’re being submerged" until it is too late. It is a thriller built on dread and obsession rather than jumpy mechanics, and that makes it linger.
good_pick_if: you want a thriller that gets colder and worse in exactly the right way
maybe_skip_if: you want relief, safety, or emotional distance

summary: The review that Brando is incredibly hot but his character is "a literal shitbag" gets the tension. The movie is scorching because it never separates desire, cruelty, and performance from one another.
good_pick_if: you want a classic powered by raw acting and unbearable tension
maybe_skip_if: you want your drama less cruel or less emotionally cornering

summary: The complaint about cutting the "sweetest Ed x Norma scenes ever" says a lot about why people like this. It is not just leftovers; it is more texture, more mood, and more of the strange human side roads that make Twin Peaks feel lived in.
good_pick_if: you already like Twin Peaks and want more of its odd side currents
maybe_skip_if: you need standalone coherence over fragments and atmosphere

summary: Criterion calling it a movie that balances tommy-gun action with "epic historical sweep" is exactly right. It moves like a crime picture but carries the sadness of an era winding itself into ruin.
good_pick_if: you want classic crime cinema with real scale and melancholy
maybe_skip_if: you want your gangster movies rougher and less old-school

summary: One good short take is that Kubrick made a "top-shelf, non-linear heist film" and people do not talk about it enough. It is mean, efficient, and built around timing so precise it becomes suspense on its own.
good_pick_if: you want a crime movie that wastes absolutely nothing
maybe_skip_if: you want your heists looser or more character-forward

summary: The line "There’s nothing more foolish than a man chasing his hat" feels like the whole movie in miniature: elegant, funny, fatalistic, and weirdly romantic about people destroying themselves over pride and loyalty.
good_pick_if: you want a crime movie with language, atmosphere, and tragic swagger
maybe_skip_if: you want cleaner plotting than Coen knotwork

summary: The funniest review angle is how "absolutely deranged" parts of it feel, but that wildness is part of the appeal. The movie is paranoid, satirical, and so nervy that its weirdness becomes a strength.
good_pick_if: you want a political thriller that feels genuinely unstable
maybe_skip_if: you want realism over nerve-jangling strangeness

summary: Calling it "Certified Copy circa 1975 with added weapons trafficking" is a joke, but it gets the identity-drift mood. This is a thriller where atmosphere, alienation, and motion matter more than any single plot beat.
good_pick_if: you want a thriller that feels like getting lost on purpose
maybe_skip_if: you want urgency and explanation over mood

summary: The joke that this is not really a thriller, "rich people just be like that," is actually a decent pitch. The movie is all ritualized desire, marital paranoia, and nighttime unease that never settles into anything safe.
good_pick_if: you want something erotic, funny, and quietly unnerving
maybe_skip_if: you want plot payoffs more than mood and implication
